questions.question: A box of mass $m$ rests on an inclined plane at angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the incline is $\mu_s$. State the condition on $\mu_s$ and $\theta$ for the box to begin sliding.
questions.answer:
Forces on the box along the incline:
- Gravity component down the slope: $mg\sin\theta$
- Maximum static friction (up the slope): $f_{s,\max} = \mu_s N = \mu_s mg\cos\theta$

The box slides when the gravitational component exceeds maximum static friction:

$mg\sin\theta > \mu_s mg\cos\theta$

$$\boxed{\mu_s < \tan\theta}$$

Equivalently, the incline angle exceeds the **angle of friction** $\phi_s = \arctan(\mu_s)$.

questions.question: A $4\ \mathrm{kg}$ block slides down a $30°$ incline with constant velocity. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the coefficient of kinetic friction, (b) the friction force, (c) the normal force.
questions.answer:
Constant velocity means zero net force.

**(c)** Normal force: $N = mg\cos 30° = 4 \times 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6\ \mathrm{N}$

**(b)** Along the incline (equilibrium): $f = mg\sin 30° = 4 \times 10 \times 0.5 = 20\ \mathrm{N}$

**(a)** $\mu_k = \dfrac{f}{N} = \dfrac{20}{20\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \tan 30° \approx 0.577$

This confirms the rule: constant-velocity sliding means $\mu_k = \tan\theta$.

questions.question: A $3\ \mathrm{kg}$ block is pushed along a horizontal floor by a horizontal force of $21\ \mathrm{N}$. The block accelerates at $3\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the friction force, (b) the coefficient of kinetic friction.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Newton's second law horizontally:

$F - f = ma \Rightarrow f = F - ma = 21 - 3 \times 3 = 21 - 9 = 12\ \mathrm{N}$

**(b)** Normal force $N = mg = 30\ \mathrm{N}$

$\mu_k = \dfrac{f}{N} = \dfrac{12}{30} = 0.4$

questions.question: Block Q (mass $m$) sits on top of block P (mass $M$) which is on a **frictionless** horizontal surface. A horizontal force $F$ is applied to P. The coefficient of kinetic friction between P and Q is $\mu$. Find: (a) the acceleration of Q, (b) the acceleration of P, (c) the time $T$ after which both blocks move at the same speed (starting from rest).
questions.answer:
Friction from P on Q acts **forward** (kinetic); friction from Q on P acts **backward** (Newton's 3rd law).

Friction force magnitude: $f = \mu mg$

**(a)** Q (only friction acts on it):

$a_Q = \dfrac{\mu mg}{m} = \mu g$

**(b)** P (net force $F - f$):

$a_P = \dfrac{F - \mu mg}{M}$

**(c)** Velocities: $v_Q = \mu g t$, $v_P = v_0 - \dfrac{\mu mg}{M}t$ (P given initial speed $v_0$, Q starts from rest). Setting equal:

$$T = \frac{Mv_0}{(M+m)\mu g}$$

(This is the standard result from the 2016 MEXT exam stacked-block problem.)

questions.question: A car of mass $1000\ \mathrm{kg}$ traveling at $20\ \mathrm{m/s}$ brakes to a stop in $4\ \mathrm{s}$ on a level road. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the deceleration, (b) the braking friction force, (c) the coefficient of kinetic friction between tires and road.

A $5\ \mathrm{kg}$ block is on a $45°$ rough incline. The coefficient of static friction is $\mu_s = 0.6$ and of kinetic friction is $\mu_k = 0.4$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. (a) Does the block slide? If it is given a small push and slides, find (b) the net force and (c) the acceleration.
questions.answer:
**(a)** $\tan 45° = 1 > \mu_s = 0.6$, so **yes, the block slides** (the gravity component exceeds maximum static friction).

**(b)** Once sliding, use kinetic friction:

$N = mg\cos 45° = 5 \times 10 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 25\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{N}$

Gravity along slope: $mg\sin 45° = 25\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{N}$

Kinetic friction (up slope): $f_k = \mu_k N = 0.4 \times 25\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2}\ \mathrm{N}$

Net force (down slope): $F_{\text{net}} = 25\sqrt{2} - 10\sqrt{2} = 15\sqrt{2} \approx 21.2\ \mathrm{N}$

**(c)** $a = F_{\text{net}}/m = 15\sqrt{2}/5 = 3\sqrt{2} \approx 4.24\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ (down the incline)

questions.question: A $2\ \mathrm{kg}$ block slides down a rough $37°$ incline from rest and travels $5\ \mathrm{m}$ in $2\ \mathrm{s}$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ and $\sin 37° = 0.6$, $\cos 37° = 0.8$. Find: (a) the acceleration, (b) the friction force, (c) the coefficient of kinetic friction.
questions.answer:
**(a)** Using $s = \frac{1}{2}at^2$ (starts from rest):

$5 = \frac{1}{2}a(4) \Rightarrow a = 2.5\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$ (down the slope)

**(b)** Along the slope (down positive):

$mg\sin\theta - f = ma$

$f = mg\sin\theta - ma = 2(10)(0.6) - 2(2.5) = 12 - 5 = 7\ \mathrm{N}$

**(c)** $N = mg\cos\theta = 2(10)(0.8) = 16\ \mathrm{N}$

$\mu_k = \dfrac{f}{N} = \dfrac{7}{16} = 0.4375 \approx 0.44$

questions.question: Two stacked blocks rest on a frictionless floor: top block A ($2\ \mathrm{kg}$), bottom block B ($6\ \mathrm{kg}$). The coefficient of static friction between A and B is $\mu_s = 0.5$. A horizontal force $F$ is applied to B. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find the maximum $F$ such that A does not slip on B.
questions.answer:
If A and B move together with acceleration $a$:

$F = (m_A + m_B)a = 8a$

For A not to slip, friction from B on A provides its entire acceleration:

$f = m_A a \leq \mu_s m_A g = 0.5 \times 2 \times 10 = 10\ \mathrm{N}$

Maximum acceleration: $a_{\max} = \dfrac{\mu_s m_A g}{m_A} = \mu_s g = 5\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$

Maximum force:

$$F_{\max} = (m_A + m_B)a_{\max} = 8 \times 5 = 40\ \mathrm{N}$$

questions.question: A block of mass $m$ on a horizontal surface is attached to a horizontal spring (spring constant $k$). The system is at rest with the spring at its natural length. The coefficient of static friction is $\mu_s$. How far can the spring be stretched before the block starts to move?
questions.answer:
The spring exerts a horizontal force $F_{\text{spring}} = kx$ on the block.

The block starts to move when this force exceeds the maximum static friction:

$kx > \mu_s mg$

Maximum stretch before sliding begins:

$$x_{\max} = \frac{\mu_s mg}{k}$$

For $x < x_{\max}$: block at rest, spring force balanced by static friction.
At $x = x_{\max}$: block is on the verge of sliding.

questions.question: A sled of mass $10\ \mathrm{kg}$ is dragged at constant speed along a horizontal snowy surface by a rope that makes an angle $20°$ above the horizontal. The coefficient of kinetic friction is $0.15$. Take $g = 10\ \mathrm{m/s^2}$. Find: (a) the normal force, (b) the tension in the rope.
questions.answer:
Let $T$ = tension. Vertical equilibrium: $N + T\sin 20° = mg$

$N = mg - T\sin 20°$

Horizontal equilibrium (constant speed): $T\cos 20° = \mu_k N = \mu_k(mg - T\sin 20°)$

$T\cos 20° = 0.15(100 - T\sin 20°)$

$T\cos 20° + 0.15T\sin 20° = 15$

$T(\cos 20° + 0.15\sin 20°) = 15$

Using $\cos 20° \approx 0.940$, $\sin 20° \approx 0.342$:

$T(0.940 + 0.051) = 15 \Rightarrow T \approx \dfrac{15}{0.991} \approx 15.1\ \mathrm{N}$

**(a)** $N = 100 - 15.1 \times 0.342 \approx 100 - 5.2 = 94.8\ \mathrm{N}$

**(b)** $T \approx 15.1\ \mathrm{N}$
